title: Chord Quadratic: Inner Product Expansion of Sphere Intersection
content: `chord_quadratic_sphere` expands the sphere equation $\|P + t \cdot \text{dir}\| = r$ into a scalar quadratic in $t$. The proof first squares both sides to get $\langle P + t \cdot \text{dir}, P + t \cdot \text{dir}\rangle = r^2$, then expands the inner product using `inner_add_left`, `inner_add_right`, `inner_smul_left`, `inner_smul_right`, and symmetry `real_inner_comm`. The `‖dir‖ = 1` hypothesis is used as `⟨dir, dir⟩ = 1` via `real_inner_self_eq_norm_mul_norm`. This expansion step is the same in any inner product space, making the rest of the proof dimension-free.
mathContext: $\|P + t\,\text{dir}\|^2 = \langle P,P\rangle + 2t\langle P,\text{dir}\rangle + t^2\langle\text{dir},\text{dir}\rangle = \|P\|^2 + 2t\langle P,\text{dir}\rangle + t^2$. Setting equal to $r^2$: $t^2 + 2t\langle P,\text{dir}\rangle + (\|P\|^2 - r^2) = 0$.

title: Vieta's Product Formula Without Explicit Roots
content: `chord_roots_product_sphere` derives $t_1 \cdot t_2 = \|P\|^2 - r^2$ without computing the roots explicitly. The proof applies `chord_quadratic_sphere` to both $t_1$ and $t_2$, then subtracts: $(t_1^2 - t_2^2) + 2(t_1 - t_2)\langle P, \text{dir}\rangle = 0$, factoring as $(t_1 - t_2)(t_1 + t_2 + 2\langle P, \text{dir}\rangle) = 0$. Since $t_1 \neq t_2$, we get $t_1 + t_2 = -2\langle P, \text{dir}\rangle$. Adding the two quadratics and combining gives $t_1^2 + t_2^2 = 4\langle P, \text{dir}\rangle^2 - 2t_1t_2$; together with $(t_1+t_2)^2 = t_1^2 + 2t_1t_2 + t_2^2$, a `linarith` closes with $t_1 t_2 = \|P\|^2 - r^2$.
mathContext: Vieta's formulas for $t^2 + bt + c = 0$: $t_1 + t_2 = -b$ and $t_1 t_2 = c$. Here $b = 2\langle P,\text{dir}\rangle$ and $c = \|P\|^2 - r^2$.

title: Interior Point Forces Opposite Signs: t₁·t₂ < 0
content: The private lemma `chord_roots_opp_signs_sphere` establishes that for an interior point ($\|P\| < r$), the chord parameters $t_1, t_2$ have opposite signs. The proof applies `chord_roots_product_sphere` to get $t_1 t_2 = \|P\|^2 - r^2$, then uses `nlinarith [norm_nonneg P]` to derive $\|P\|^2 < r^2$ from $\|P\| < r$, giving $t_1 t_2 < 0$. This sign fact is crucial: it transforms $|t_1| \cdot |t_2| = |t_1 t_2| = -(t_1 t_2)$ from signed to unsigned product.
mathContext: $\|P\| < r \Rightarrow \|P\|^2 < r^2 \Rightarrow t_1 t_2 = \|P\|^2 - r^2 < 0$. Geometrically: an interior point is between the two chord endpoints, so one parameter is positive and one negative along any direction.

title: Power of a Point: Invariance Across All Secant Lines
content: `sphere_power_invariant` combines the Vieta product and sign analysis to prove $|t_1| \cdot |t_2| = r^2 - \|P-O\|^2$. The proof translates to $Q = P - O$ (centering at origin), applies `chord_roots_product_sphere` and `chord_roots_opp_signs_sphere`, then uses `abs_mul`, `abs_of_neg`, and `ring` to convert the signed product to unsigned. `sphere_chord_products_equal` then proves the chord product is independent of direction: two calls to `sphere_power_invariant` with different directions both give $r^2 - \|P-O\|^2$, completing the equality.
mathContext: $|t_1| \cdot |t_2| = |t_1 t_2| = -(t_1 t_2) = -(\|P-O\|^2 - r^2) = r^2 - \|P-O\|^2$. This is Steiner's *power of a point*: a real number depending only on $P$, $O$, and $r$, invariant under rotation of the secant.

title: Sphere3D: Explicit 3D Corollary
content: `Sphere3D` bundles center, radius, and positivity into a structure for `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`. `sphere3d_chord_products_equal` states the result in terms of actual geometric distances: $\|A_1 - P\| \cdot \|A_2 - P\| = \|B_1 - P\| \cdot \|B_2 - P\|$. The proof converts: $\|A_i - P\| = \|s_i \cdot d\| = |s_i|$ using `norm_smul`, `Real.norm_eq_abs`, and `hd₁, mul_one`. Then the `onSphere` conditions are converted to parametric form using `abel`. Finally, `sphere_chord_products_equal` closes the goal. This demonstrates that `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)` is an `InnerProductSpace ℝ` instance, so the general theorem specializes.
